newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica shares seen edgy next week ahead of budget.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica shares seen edgy next week ahead of budget.

text.p: South Africa's share market is expected to be volatile next week as the country's 1997/98 budget draws nearer although analysts say the underlying mood will remain bullish, underpinned by positive economic fundamentals.
Analysts said market perceptions were that the currency market would fluctuate next week on growing uncertainties towards the March 12 budget and this might induce more buying in industrials.
"I see the market continuing up and down. I can only see volatility," Gad Ariovich, investment strategy manager at SMK Securities told Reuters.

"It's coming nearer to the budget. I feel that a lot of the perception of the rand is based on what will be the new exchange regulations. I can see some fluctuations on the rand and so people may buy more industrials and rand hedged shares," he said.
"Perhaps foreigners will want to push the rand weaker next week on these (budget) uncertainties...this will help metals and the gold board," said John Winship, BOE Asset Management managing director.
The gold and metals sectors were expected to remain the flavour of the month next week, particularly if gold's retracement of its recent losses continued.
On Friday morning, gold fixed at $350.75 in London, its highest fixing since January 29, against $345 on Thursday afternoon.

The market was also likely to keep an eye on Wall Street after its steep losses on Wednesday and Thursday this week, although traders noted that the Dow had had little impact on the local market recently.
"I don't think we should tie ourselves entirely to Wall Street," one trader who asked not to be identified said.
"The market is still positive despite Wall Street...We have seen some volatility over the past few days. I think that volatility will continue but the trend should be upwards," an analyst said.

Societe Generale Frankel Pollak director Johan Marais said he expected the market to continue consolidating in the week ahead, as sentiment was underpinned by recent bullish comments by monetary authorities.
"We are seeing a consolidation phase before we go further. I'm very bullish across the board because of the economic news coming out at the moment," Marais said.

Traders said the market had been reassured by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's pre-budget roadshow on Thursday, particularly his comments that government was on course to meet its budget deficit targets.
Analysts noted that the market would also be watching a host of economic data expected next week.

January trade data will be released on Tuesday, while January consumer inflation and fourth quarter gross domestic product will be released on Thursday, as will January money supply and private sector credit extension data.
